dedupe_keys.name: powerpath time explicit disruption and recovery model of interdependent road and electricity systems

description: PowerPath is a critical infrastructure risk, resilience and adaptation model that represents the coupled behaviour of electricity substations and the road network during and after a pluvial flood. At each hourly time step it simulates flood exposure, substation failure through a depth-damage curve, road accessibility, allocation of a set number of repair crews and recovery, and maps the resulting impacts to the population and value of lost load in each substation's service area. The sample use case covers the province of South Holland in the Netherlands, using a 200 mm rainfall pluvial flood scenario from the province's open data portal, medium-low voltage substations published by the distribution operator Stedin, OpenStreetMap roads and CBS population data; runs are repeated to explore uncertainty. It was developed by Daniel Peregrina Gonzalez and Lieke Meijer at Deltares in the EU Horizon Europe MIRACA project (grant 101093854), continues the ci_adapt code of 2025, and was released on Zenodo on 17 June 2026 under CC BY 4.0 (the repository LICENSE is MIT) as Python notebooks with sample data, about 315 MB. Caveats: hazard, population and land use data are sampled because full files are too large, and results depend on fragility slope and crew assumptions. It supports cascading failure, emergency response and climate adaptation analysis for distribution network operators; a related record is the MIRACA pan-European critical infrastructure exposure data.
